purpose: run containers reliably at scale with scheduling, networking, configuration and safe updates managed by the platform
entry_criteria: Container images and their requirements are known
A cluster exists with defined environments
Platform standards for namespaces, quotas and policies exist
procedure: Define workloads declaratively with resource requests and limits, health probes and a rolling update strategy.
Separate configuration and secrets from images; mount secrets from the secret store, never in manifests.
Apply network policies, a non-root security context and pod security standards.
Set disruption budgets and spread replicas across failure domains.
Deploy through the pipeline from version control (no manual kubectl in production) and verify rollout status.
Observe and tune: resource use, restarts, scheduling failures.
acceptance_criteria: Every workload has resource limits and probes
Security context and network policies are applied
Replicas are spread across failure domains

validation.command: kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f k8s/ && kubectl rollout status deployment/app

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: The service runs three replicas spread across zones with readiness probes, a pod disruption budget of one, and a rolling update that never takes more than one pod down at a time.
